problemStatement: A financial surface must show something before any account is connected. The number zero and the absence of data are different claims, and a surface that renders them identically tells the user something false.
whyThisProblem: Trial 1's build rendered a fabricated figure labelled 'your Square export'. The salon product's first screen has the same hazard in its mildest form: before a connector exists, every metric is unbound, and $0 is the most believable wrong answer available.
licenceNote: Records our observations of publicly listed reference screens. No source pixels are stored, cached, indexed or embedded. Each record cites its canonical Mobbin URL so the source can be re-inspected rather than reproduced.

observations.surface: analytics dashboard, no bank account connected

facts.subject: primary chart panel
facts.locatorDescription: large upper panel; chart area is a greyed skeleton, overlaid with centred text

facts.subject: primary chart panel
facts.property: words of explanation for the absence
facts.locatorDescription: 'No data available' plus 'Connect your bank account to unlock this metric.'

facts.subject: secondary metric tiles
facts.locatorDescription: lower row; 'Average Monthly Burn Rate $0' and 'Average Monthly Expenses $0', typeset identically to a measured value

facts.subject: secondary metric tiles
facts.locatorDescription: no marker, tooltip, or caption adjacent to either $0

observations.observedTension: One screen answers the same question two ways. The upper panel treats unbound as unrenderable and says why; the lower tiles render $0 in the typography of a measurement. A reader who scrolls past the explanation sees two confident zeros.
observations.boundary: Static screen capture. Whether the $0 tiles change after connecting, or carry a state not visible here, was not observed.

facts.subject: screen body
facts.locatorDescription: centred illustration, one sentence, one button; no figure anywhere in the content area

facts.subject: absence statement
facts.property: names the object rather than the system
facts.locatorDescription: single sentence directly above the primary action

facts.subject: primary action
facts.locatorDescription: 'CONNECT ACCOUNT' is the only interactive control in the content area

observations.boundary: Does not tell the user what they will see after connecting, so the value of the action is unstated.

facts.subject: absence statement
facts.locatorDescription: 'You don't have any bank accounts connected' — states the user's situation, not the system's failure to load

facts.subject: page title
facts.value: 'Connected bank accounts' remains as the heading
facts.locatorDescription: top of content area, unchanged by the empty state

observations.boundary: This is a management surface, not a metric surface, so it never had a number to withhold. Weaker evidence for the metric case than Quicken.

facts.subject: headline revenue figure
facts.property: carries a definition of the metric
facts.value: tooltip states 'Revenue represents your total income from all sources'

facts.subject: headline revenue figure
facts.value: 'If the revenue appears too high, internal transfers may have been marked as income'

facts.subject: headline revenue figure
facts.value: 'You can fix this by excluding the transactions from the calculations'

facts.subject: comparison baseline
facts.locatorDescription: directly beneath the headline figure, smaller type

observations.observedTension: This is a bound figure that still discloses how it can mislead. The disclosure is about the metric's DEFINITION, not its data source — a distinct axis from whether the data is real.
observations.boundary: Whether the tooltip appears on hover only was not determined from the capture; a disclosure reachable only by hover is weaker than one always visible.
